args.message:
Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money (FIN-212)

round_money claimed banker's rounding in its docstring but used
ROUND_HALF_UP, causing tests/test_money.py to fail in the nightly build.

args.head: fix/fin-212-banker-rounding
args.title: Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money (FIN-212)
args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` was documented as using banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212) but was implemented with `ROUND_HALF_UP`. This caused `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` to fail in the nightly build.

This PR switches the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. No other changes.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986`: passed.
- Test expectations: `2.675 -> 2.68` and `2.665 -> 2.66` match ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

Note: this changes rounding for exact-half cases in production code paths that call `round_money`, so reviewers should confirm this matches the intended FIN-212 behavior.

content.text: I'll start by reading the source and the test to see what's expected.

The test matches ROUND_HALF_EVEN: 2.675 rounds to 2.68 (7 is odd, so it rounds to the even 8), and 2.665 rounds to 2.66 (6 is already even). The bug is that `src/money.py` uses ROUND_HALF_UP. I'll create the branch and make that one-line change.
